reference: Bash metadata contracts; read-only check compared byte-for-byte through a deliberate Python resource.getrlimit adapter. Locking and global policy operations require future mocks.
coverage: Bash classifies mlock as a builtin using type -t.
Bash help metadata advertises the five documented subcommands and the loadable description.
Deferred operational scenarios specify controlled conditions for all, unlock, check, try-lock, and ptrace-scope.
Operation: read-only check formatting against an independent getrlimit adapter.
exclusions: No GNU mlock CLI parity claim.
Lock/unlock and global ptrace policy operations remain deferred with specific future mocks.

cases.purpose: Verify through Bash's type builtin that the selected mlock loadable is available as a builtin.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t mlock) == builtin ]] || exit 1
printf '%s\n' 'mlock type: builtin'

cases.purpose: Verify Bash help exposes the documented description and every advertised mlock subcommand without invoking an operation.
cases.script:
doc=$(help mlock)
[[ $doc == *'Pin/unpin process memory to prevent swap leakage of secrets.'* ]] || exit 1
for verb in all unlock check try-lock ptrace-scope; do
  [[ $doc == *"mlock $verb"* ]] || exit 1
done
printf '%s\n' 'mlock help documents all five subcommands'
cases.stdout: mlock help documents all five subcommands

cases.purpose: Validate mlockall(MCL_CURRENT|MCL_FUTURE) success and its RLIMIT_MEMLOCK failure path, including whether failure leaves process state unchanged.
cases.reason: The failure paths need no privilege and have no fixture. The success path needs a per-case RLIMIT_MEMLOCK at least as large as the shell's mapped size. Raising the hard limit needs CAP_SYS_RESOURCE (setrlimit returns EPERM under uid 2000), so the fixture cannot set it itself. RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in both the legacy runner and the plain driver is inherited from the guest default (kernel default 8 MiB, not pinned by either driver). Lowering it with `ulimit -l` is unprivileged. Raising the hard limit needs CAP_SYS_RESOURCE, which only the root controller holds. Not a privilege block for the fixture: the guest controller already runs as root and sets rlimits in terminal.child_limits before setuid(2000), so a per-case RLIMIT_MEMLOCK option there is a small existing-driver extension (root-owned), not a new privileged driver.

cases.purpose: Verify munlockall releases a known locked mapping and does not leave locked pages after the call.
cases.reason: Seeding needs the same per-case RLIMIT_MEMLOCK driver option as all-operation, because raising the hard limit returns EPERM without CAP_SYS_RESOURCE. The no-lock and injected-error paths need no privilege. No fixture exists. Not a privilege block for the fixture: the guest controller already runs as root and sets rlimits in terminal.child_limits before setuid(2000), so a per-case RLIMIT_MEMLOCK option there is a small existing-driver extension (root-owned), not a new privileged driver.

cases.purpose: Read-only process RLIMIT_MEMLOCK formatting compared with Python getrlimit; no locked pages or limits change.
cases.script: if [[ $(type -t mlock) == builtin ]]; then mlock check; else /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import resource; a,b=resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_MEMLOCK); f=lambda n:'"'"'unlimited'"'"' if n==resource.RLIM_INFINITY else str(n); print('"'"'soft='"'"'+f(a)+'"'"' hard='"'"'+f(b))'; fi

cases.purpose: Exercise the bounded anonymous mapping probe on successful lock/unlock, the 1-byte and 1-MiB boundaries, malformed sizes, and an insufficient-limit failure with cleanup.
cases.reason: Not a capability block. Every path is reachable by lowering RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in the fixture itself under the default limit. No fixture exists.

cases.purpose: Check parsing and descriptions for Yama ptrace_scope levels 0 through 3, unknown numeric levels, and unavailable or malformed procfs data.
cases.reason: Not a capability block. The live read can be checked now, and controlled contents need only RUNNER-BINDS: a per-side bind mount of fixture files over /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope inside a USERNS mount namespace in the plain driver. A preflight must confirm that the kernel allows a procfs file overmount from a user namespace; if it does not, the fallback is a controller-made bind (CAP_SYS_ADMIN held by the root controller). Writing the real sysctl (global, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, level 3 irreversible) is neither needed nor safe. No fixture exists.
